answer: The comet counter is kept in quartz and island makes public each threshold crossing. An answer is only accepted from an identity that has already had 5 attestations accepted by others, which means the first thing a new alias must do is earn trust rather than claim reward. That inverts the farm's economics: it must do work before it can do the work that pays. Every extra alias adds 12 hours of verification and 15 percent more locked value. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
